title: defineRegressionLoss — defineRegressionLoss
text: Returns torch::nn_module computes one four common regression losses prediction tensor target tensor. returned object passed directly loss argument luz::setup(). four supported loss types : "mse" Mean Squared Error. $$\frac{1}{n}\sum_{}(\hat{y}_i - y_i)^2$$ Penalises large errors quadratically. Sensitive outliers squared term magnifies large residuals. "mae" Mean Absolute Error. $$\frac{1}{n}\sum_{}|\hat{y}_i - y_i|$$ robust outliers MSE. gradient constant magnitude non-zero residuals, can slow convergence near optimum. "huber" Huber loss. $$L_\delta(r) = \begin{cases}       \tfrac{1}{2}r^2 & |r| \le \delta \\       \delta\bigl(|r| - \tfrac{1}{2}\delta\bigr) & |r| > \delta     \end{cases}$$ \(r = \hat{y} - y\). Quadratic small residuals (like MSE) linear large residuals (like MAE), combining outlier robustness smooth gradients near zero. transition point set delta. "log_cosh" Log-Cosh loss. $$\frac{1}{n}\sum_{}\log\!\bigl(\cosh(\hat{y}_i - y_i)\bigr)$$ Approximates \(\tfrac{1}{2}r^2\) small residuals \(|r| - \log 2\) large residuals. Doubly differentiable everywhere, benefits second-order optimisers produces smooth loss surfaces. Computed numerically stable form: \(|r| + \log(1 + e^{-2|r|}) - \log 2\).
